note: The reading taken for every entry of the Select Agents and Toxins List as codified at 2024-06-01 (42 CFR 73.3, 73.4; 9 CFR 121.3; 7 CFR 331.3 — 9 CFR 121.4 duplicates 42 CFR 73.4 and is dropped). Curation decides the taxon and the pinned 2023-04-01 NCBI taxonomy only validates it: name matching against names.dmp resolves several entries into the wrong kingdom. The one entry where descent is refused. The pinned taxonomy has no 'SARS coronavirus' species: the containing node is 694009, 'Severe acute respiratory syndrome-related coronavirus', whose 222 children include SARS-CoV-2 (2697049). The regulation lists SARS-CoV and does not list SARS-CoV-2 — it regulates SARS-CoV/SARS-CoV-2 chimeras separately, which only makes sense if SARS-CoV-2 is not itself listed. Descending would therefore import the largest viral sequence space in UniProt on the strength of a node name, inflating the denylist and overstating what the filter should have removed. Taken as the named node without descent; the per-strain alternative is noted in D-137 and declined because it would miss SARS-CoV isolates absent from the 2023-04 dump.

Not a taxon as worded. The name resolves to Influenza A virus (11320) as an equivalent name, and descending it takes in tens of thousands of strain nodes including human seasonal influenza, which the regulation does not list. The regulation's own scope is a virulence criterion on the isolate — a sequence-level property with no taxonomic expression at all, which is a §A0 under-specification finding in the list rather than in ESM3. Taken as Influenza A virus with descent, the widest of the three readings, because for an audit of a safeguard an over-inclusive denylist overstates what should have been removed rather than understating it. D-137 records the two narrower readings declined.
